title: Who has to say yes?
intro: It depends on how you enter the market. Choose the one that fits, and step through the gates on the way.
link_label: See what a Readiness Assessment covers
note: The order varies from company to company. What does not vary is that each of them asks before saying yes.

paths.label: We sell AI to the established players

gates.name: Procurement
gates.who: The buyer's purchasing function. It decides whether you get as far as a contract.
questions: Which AI systems are in the product, and who answers for each of them?
How is the system classified under the EU AI Act?
Which models and sub-suppliers do you depend on?
gates.assessment: your EU AI Act classification, and an AI Compass baseline built around these questions.

gates.name: Security review
gates.who: The buyer's security and privacy function. It can stop a deal that everyone else wants.
questions: Who can reach models, data and APIs, and is that access logged?
Which personal data is processed, where, and with what minimisation?
Can you show evidence, and not only a policy?
gates.assessment: the seven criteria for misuse and dual-use risk, including access control, data and supply chain.

gates.name: Investor
gates.who: The institutional investor in your next round, doing due diligence.
questions: What is the regulatory exposure, and who owns it in the company?
Would the company get through a large customer's review?
Are decisions made with clear owners, documented reasoning and a working board?
gates.assessment: the 6Sense screening, where Risk and Decision are two of the six dimensions.

gates.name: Regulator
gates.who: You become the regulated party yourself. The supervisor asks before you are allowed to operate.
questions: Who answers for each AI system, and how is it classified under the EU AI Act?
Do people have the final say in decisions that affect individuals, and is that logged?
How are model changes and incidents recorded and reviewed?
gates.assessment: your EU AI Act classification, and an AI Compass baseline that shows where the evidence is missing.

gates.name: Partner
gates.who: The bank, insurer or platform you build on. Its own obligations are passed on to you.
questions: Can we rely on you without breaching our own requirements?
Which sub-suppliers do you depend on, and what happens if one of them fails?
Can you produce evidence when we ask for it, within days?
gates.assessment: the seven criteria for misuse and dual-use risk, including access control, data and supply chain.

gates.name: Investor
gates.who: The institutional investor in your next round, doing due diligence.
questions: What is the regulatory exposure, and who owns it in the company?
Would the company get through the regulator's and the partner's review?
Are decisions made with clear owners, documented reasoning and a working board?
gates.assessment: the 6Sense screening, where Risk and Decision are two of the six dimensions.
